newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-RONALDO PENALTY GIVES BARCELONA DESERVED CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO PENALTY GIVES BARCELONA DESERVED CUP WIN.

text.p: A first-half penalty coolly converted by Brazilian world footballer of the year Ronaldo gave Barcelona a deserved 1-0 win over holders Paris Saint Germain in an exciting European Cup Winners' Cup final on Wednesday.

The only goal of a match that could easily have finished with a bigger scoreline came after 37 minutes when Ronaldo picked himself up after being hauled down by Bruno N'Gotty in the box and wrong-footed PSG goalkeeper Bernard Lama from the spot.

Ronaldo's 33rd goal of the season proved enough to give Barcelona the cup for a record fourth time, condemned PSG to enter the record books as the eighth holders to fail to retain the trophy the following year and proved to N'Gotty how cruel soccer can be.
Last season he was PSG's hero with the only goal when they beat Rapid Vienna to win the cup.

The victory kept Barcelona on course for what could be a glorious haul of four trophies this season. They added the Cup Winners' Cup to the Spanish Super Cup and they meet Real Betis in the Spanish Cup final later this month. They also retain an outside chance of pipping Real Madrid for the Spanish league title.
The only thing they look certain to lose is English coach Bobby Robson who seems set to leave the Camp Nou because of the club's internal politics rather than any lack of silverware.

Barcelona appeared to take the lead after 27 minutes when Portuguese defender Fernando Couto turned a header from a Josep Guardiola corner under Bernard Lama's crossbar. But their celebrations were immediately cut short as German referee Markus Merk ruled that Barcelona skipper Gheorghe Popescu had fouled midfielder Benoit Cauet.

But 10 minutes later there was no doubt about Barcelona's goal. A clever Barcelona build-up involving Sergi, Ivan de la Pena and Luis Enrique came to an abrupt and illegal end when N'Gotty clattered into Ronaldo in the box to concede what proved to be the decisive penalty.

PSG, starting the match with seven of the team that won the cup last year, went close to equalising after 58 minutes when Patrice Loko shot against a post but Leonardo blasted the rebound over the bar.

PSG, with Rai involved in almost everything in midfield and Laurent Fournier driving his side forward with some penetrating runs, created several more scoring chances but most were restricted to long-range efforts as the Barcelona defence, well marshalled by Abelardo and Couto, stood firm.
Cauet went close however with an angled drive from only eight metres out after 50 minutes which Vitor Baia in the Barcelona goal did well to palm away.
Barcelona had two good chances to increase their lead in the second half. Amor, a half-time substitute for the injured Popescu went close with a 25-metre drive that just sailed over the bar.
Then in the dying minutes Ronaldo set Luis Figo up for what seemed a certain goal. But with Lama beaten, Figo could only watch as the ball bounced away off the crossbar.
